title: Data Model Objects (DMOs) & Data Lake Objects (DLOs)

html:
The Data 360 canonical data model is what makes a pile of ingested files queryable as a business. This phase covers Data Lake Objects vs Data Model Objects, the standard Customer 360 entities (Individual, Contact Points, Account), primary-key strategy, field mapping, and the schema-design decisions the exam tests hardest.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Explain the DLO → DMO relationship and why the separation exists.
  • Name the core standard DMOs and their hierarchy: Individual, ContactPointEmail, ContactPointPhone, UnifiedIndividual, Account.
  • Select primary keys and define relationships between DMOs.
  • Map source fields to the canonical model and choose when a custom DMO is needed.
  • Design a schema for SLA/loyalty tracking and reason about one-to-many vs many-to-many shapes.

1. DLO vs DMO — the two-layer model

Think of the pipeline as two shelves:

text
sources → [ DLO raw, one per stream ] → mapping & transforms → [ DMO canonical ] → profiles/segments/insights
             DataLakeObject              (harmonization)        DataModelObject
Data Lake Object (DLO)Data Model Object (DMO)
PurposeRaw landing zoneNormalised, canonical business object
Created byData stream (Phase 2)Field mapping + transforms
ShapeSource schema as-isStandard Customer 360 schema (or custom)
Suffix_dlm (e.g. Web_Visit__dlm)_dlm too (e.g. Individual__dlm), or standard/DMO names
Consumersmapping, transformscalculated insights, segments, activation, apps
Best exam answer"Where does raw data land?" → DLO"Where do you query unified customer data?" → DMO (UnifiedIndividual)

Classic exam line: after ingestion, data is stored in the DLO; after harmonization, the queried power comes from the DMO. Do not blur them.

2. The Standard Customer 360 Data Model

The canonical model revolves around the Individual (person) entity and its Contact Points. Salesforce ships a rich set of standard DMOs; master the core seven:

text
UnifiedIndividual (UnifiedIndividual__dlm)
   ├── Individual                      (Individual__dlm)       person source
   ├── Contact Point Email             (ContactPointEmail__dlm) email address
   ├── Contact Point Phone             (ContactPointPhone__dlm) phone number
   ├── Contact Point Address           (ContactPointAddress__dlm) physical address
   ├── Account                         (Account__dlm)          company/business
   └── Individual ↔ Account            (Individual__dlm.AccountId-ish link)

Other DMOs you will see repeatedly: ContactPointSocial, Entitlement, EntitlementRule, Case, Opportunity, Order, Lead, Product, ServiceResource, Activity/Engagement. Marketing-specific: MarketingActivity, Campaign, Audience.

Linking to the CRM

Mapping doesn't duplicate CRM data — it creates DMOs that mirror CRM objects (Case__dlm, Opportunity__dlm). The sfdc_ prefix fields (e.g. sfdc_recordId) hold the original Salesforce record IDs and are how data flows back to the CRM through activations and data actions.

3. Primary Keys and Relationships

PK strategy

Every DMO needs a primary key (Id, often sfdc_id or a business key). Gold rules:

  1. Use a stable external key from the source when one exists (customer_id).
  2. When the source lacks one, compose it (brand + store + ticket_no).
  3. The key you choose at the DLO/ DMO level directly feeds identity resolution (Phase 4) — a weak key = unresolvable profiles.
  4. Never make the PK mutable business data that changes (email addresses change; use a stable person id and keep email on a Contact Point).

Relationship types in DMOs

Data 360 supports standard relational shapes on DMOs:

  • One-to-many: an Individual has many Contact Point Emails — model ContactPointEmail.IndividualId.
  • Many-to-many: Individuals to Accounts (a consultant at two companies) — modelled with a linking/association object (like a junction in the CRM).
  • Mandatory vs optional: which side must exist (e.g. a Contact Point requires an Individual for a good profile).

Relationship fields are what let calculated-insight SQL JOIN DMOs (Phase 5) and let data graphs traverse Individual → CatalogEngagement → CartEngagement (Phase 14).

4. Field Mapping and Harmonization

Building the DMO from the DLO is point-and-click heavy but conceptually simple: map every field the business needs from the source shape to the canonical shape, transforming values where types/labelling differ.

Mapping decisions you'll make:

DecisionExampleConsequence of getting it wrong
Which fields mapmap total_amt and currency, skip internal_noteMissing insight dimensions; wasted DTO
Type coercionsource string "3.74" → mapped NumberIngestion mapping errors
Rename/normalisecust_id → IndividualIdDownstream joins fail silently
Enrichment (later)attach calculated lifetime_spendYou must build an insight instead

Custom DMOs

The standard model covers a lot, but you will regularly build custom DMOs for domain data (e.g. LoyaltyProfile__dlm, ProductRecommendation__dlm). Choose carefully:

  • Use a custom DMO when the entity has no sensible standard home (a loyalty tier, a prediction score).
  • Prefer standard DMOs for things the canonical model already expresses (emails, phones, addresses).
  • Mapping into standard DMOs keeps you compatible with Marketing Cloud activations and Agentforce data graphs; custom DMOs still work but require more explicit setup everywhere downstream.

5. Schema Design for a Service/SLA Lab

Your lab org mirrors this with CRM-side objects (SLA_Compliance__c, Consent_Preference__c, Segment_Sync_Log__c, Activation_Audit__c). The Data 360 equivalent for a hardware-support scenario (Phase 17, UC2):

text
PROPOSED DMO LAYOUT (conceptual)
  UnifiedIndividual__dlm          -- resolved customer
    -- orders:      Order__dlm (Order__dlm.IndividualId)       1:N
    -- devices:     Device__dlm (Device__dlm.IndividualId)     1:N
    -- warranty:    Entitlement__dlm (Entitlement__dlm.DeviceId, .OrderId) 1:1/1:N
    -- sla events:  MilestoneCase__dlm (MilestoneCase__dlm.EntitlementId) 1:N

Design questions the exam loves:

  1. Should Device be 1:1 with OrderItem or its own DMO? → its own DMO, because a device outlives a single order (warranty, repairs).
  2. Where does the SLA clock live? → on the entitlement/milestone DMO, because it is a property of the contract, not the customer.
  3. Who "owns" the record? → one Id per DMO; the IndividualId linkage is a relationship, not an owner.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: DLO/DMO sort

Classify each item: POS CSV landed rows / Unified Individual / Contact Point Email DMO / webinar event payload / loyalty tier lookup. Mark DLO or DMO and justify in one sentence each.

Exercise 2: Design the schema for the retail UC

For UC1 (Phase 17): propose DMOs for order, product, loyalty profile; give each a PK and its relationship to UnifiedIndividual__dlm. Compare with the "correct" answer in Phase 18.

Exercise 3: Mapping table

Write the mapping table from POS_Sales__dlm fields → target DMO fields for: customer_email, store_id, total, currency, order_no, item_count. Decide transforms (type coercion, rename, compose key) and note which mapping decision reduces the risk of duplicate profiles.

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
DMOData Model Object — normalised canonical data shape built from DLO data.
DLOData Lake Object — raw ingested shape, one per stream.
Canonical modelThe standard Customer 360 entity schema (Individual, Contact Points, Account…).
IndividualThe person entity in the canonical model.
Unified IndividualThe resolved, deduplicated person profile after identity resolution.
Contact PointA way to reach an Individual (email, phone, address, social).
PK / external keyThe field that uniquely identifies a record for upsert and identity.
sfdc_recordIdField holding the originating Salesforce record id to link back to CRM.
HarmonizationMapping + transforming DLO data into canonical DMO shape.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can contrast DLO and DMO with a "land vs query" frame.
  • I can draw the Individual → Contact Points → Unified Individual hierarchy.
  • I can choose and compose primary keys and justify with identity in mind.
  • I can define when to build a custom DMO vs. reuse a standard one.
  • I can design a DMO layout for an SLA/hardware scenario and defend it.
  • I can read a field-mapping table and spot the schema-change risk in it.
